body.statement:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\). It then tests every structural chart for emptiness. If the margin test fails or every chart is empty, \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\), and the input is reported as incompatible and is not rigid under \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\). Otherwise one sampled point \(x_0\) is used in the unequal-target feasibility test on every chart, and \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\) if and only if every such refinement is empty. For design B, all structural charts are first tested for emptiness; if all are empty, \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\) and the input is reported as incompatible and non-rigid, while on a nonempty union \(\lvert\mathcal T_B(p)\rvert=1\) if and only if every chartwise unequal-target refinement from the common sample \(x_0\) is empty. These are finite observable rank, support, incidence, residual-forest, cycle, and target-agreement tests.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data. For rational \(\zeta\), the encoding may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval. Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\). If both selected cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity claim is made for a witness on a boundary face. Connected-component descriptions are optional diagnostics and are not part of the rigidity decision.
body.justification: The theorem is the necessary-and-sufficient causal classifier, with strict design-A margin validation before any compatibility declaration or lift.
body.gap: Regular inversion does not decide global constancy across disconnected charts and support faces or distinguish an invalid supplied margin from a feasible normalized cycle factorization.
body.consumer: Analysts receive one exact target, legal target-changing SCM twins, or a separate incompatibility report.
body.proof_tex:
In design A, \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\neq\varnothing. \tag{15}
\]
Thus an invalid supplied margin must be rejected even if the normalized cycle charts are nonempty. In design B, the surjectivity assertion of \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\neq\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\neq\varnothing. \tag{16}
\]
Because an empty target set has cardinality zero, the failures in (15)--(16) are incompatible and non-rigid under \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}rigidity}\).

On a nonempty fiber, the same lift lemma preserves the target and is onto, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},\\
 \mathcal T_B(p)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{17}
\]
The structural equalities in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) replace each cycle fiber in (17) by the finite union of its charts. Its one-sample/all-chart equivalence (14) then proves that the relevant set in (17) is a singleton exactly when every chartwise unequal-target refinement is empty. This establishes necessity and sufficiency, including disconnected charts and comparisons across support faces, without connected-component enumeration.

The mixed-support theorem also proves the stated field-relative output discipline. If a refinement is feasible, it supplies cycle points \(x_0,x_1\) with unequal values. Equation (17) and the cycle-to-SCM lift turn these into legal full SCMs with the same observed input and, in design A, the same supplied \(m\). If both points satisfy all strict inequalities of interior support charts, \(\mathrm{lem:interior\text{-}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}positive\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) makes every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability, and selection probability strictly interior. That lemma makes no such assertion when either witness lies on a support face, so the boundary qualification is exact.
